title: The Last Five Years
events_chronological: Jamie, a young novelist, meets Cathy and is elated to be with a woman from entirely outside the world he grew up in.
Cathy and Jamie's first evening together ends with her telling him about the man she nearly settled for.
Jamie's first novel is taken by a publisher and he celebrates before he has even finished telling her.
Cathy sits through an audition in New York at which nobody behind the table looks up from their papers.
Jamie gives Cathy a present and promises her he will never walk away from her.
Cathy takes a summer job at a theatre in Ohio and writes home from a bare rented room.
Jamie's book becomes a success and he is feted at parties Cathy refuses to attend.
Cathy tells Jamie he has never once come to see her in anything.
Jamie is propositioned by a young woman at a publishing party and talks himself into it.
Cathy admits to herself that she cannot be glad about her husband's success.
Jamie sleeps with someone else and concedes to himself that the marriage is finished.
Jamie writes a letter, leaves his key on the table and lets himself out.
Cathy comes home to the empty flat and reads the letter.
syuzhet_notes: The two characters never share a scene except the wedding. His songs run forward from the first date to the last morning; hers run backward from the last morning to the first date. Told-order bullet 7 is the wedding, where the two strands cross, and after it each continues in its own direction.
fabula_notes: Chronology is recoverable because each song is dated within the five years. The wedding is the one event both strands occupy.
